Episodes 1 to 8 of 18 are authored: 494 entities, 3,104 exact mentions in original-en and 3,137 in modern-en, 492 of the 494 bound in the older edition and 491 in the modern one, 79 focused tests passing, content revision 2026-09-15.8. NEXT: episode 9 (Scylla and Charybdis, 482 paragraphs), the library and the Shakespeare argument. 4,822 paragraphs remain; the long ones are 15 (Circe, 1,441), 17 (Ithaca, 654), 11 (Sirens, 635), 12 (566) and 10 (546); episode 18 (Penelope) is eight paragraphs of monologue and will be the densest in the book.

THE RULE THAT GOVERNS THIS BOOK: A SURNAME IS ALMOST NEVER ONE MAN, SO KEY BY DEFAULT AND ALIAS ONLY ON PROOF. There is no 'Bloom' default and 4:38 -- SLIEVE BLOOM, the mountains in Offaly -- is deliberately not keyed. THE SURNAME DEDALUS CHANGES HANDS AT EPISODE 6: episodes 1-2 key it to STEPHEN, episode 6 to his father SIMON. EPISODE 7 HAS BOTH MEN IN IT -- 7:21 and 7:109-7:168 are Simon, 7:258 and 7:497 are his son. Episode 8 has only Simon (8:9, 8:141) and Stephen is not in it at all. Other sharp cases so far: TWO O'CONNELLS in one paragraph (6:330); LEOPOLD is Bloom at 5:67, THE DUKE OF ALBANY at 5:121 and THE ARCHDUKE at 8:255; PETER is three men in six paragraphs (5:95, 5:100, 5:107); BUSHE is three men in two paragraphs (7:382); TWO PENELOPES one line apart (7:519-7:520); TWO PARNELLS in one episode (8:134/8:141 Charles Stewart, 8:140/8:198 his brother John Howard); COFFEY is the priest in episode 6 and THE BUTCHER at 8:255; HANLON is the milkman at 4:13 and MICKY HANLON the fishmonger at 8:255; BEAUFOY is Philip at 8:87 and MRS PUREFOY under a slip of the tongue at 8:85.

A GUARD TRAP WORTH REMEMBERING: the alias guard is (?<![A-Za-z])...(?![A-Za-z]) for keyed tables but (?<!\w)...(?!\w) for aliases, and an APOSTROPHE IS NOT A WORD CHARACTER, so an alias 'Flynn' would bind every O'FLYNN in the book and 'Bergan' every O'BERGAN. Bare FLYNN is therefore keyed paragraph by paragraph in episode 8 and Father O'Flynn at 8:198 has his own pattern.

THE MODERN EDITION IS A REWRITE AND CHANGES THE CAST OF A PARAGRAPH IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It DELETES names (Chrysostomos 1:9, Mercury 1:293, Loyola 1:101, Adam Findlater and Dan Tallon 4:37, Hanlon 4:13, Wren 6:204, the Joe Miller 7:293) and SUPPLIES names Joyce did not write (Aristotle 3:0, Brian Boru 3:57, Deasy 3:10, Queen Victoria 3:94, M'Coy 5:27, Daniel O'Connell 6:106/6:277/6:278, Madame Bloom 6:104, Shakespeare 6:333, Martha 6:386, Nannetti 7:42 and 7:62, Bloom 7:67, Patrick Dignam 7:99, Gallaher 7:358, Mario 7:27, Long John Fanning 7:45, Boylan 8:35 and 8:255, Lot's wife 8:35, Charles Stewart Parnell 8:141, Reuben J. Dodd 8:12 and 8:364, the blind man 8:360). IT ALSO SPLITS JOYCE'S COMPOUNDS, which makes a name bindable that was not: 'Jesusmario' (7:27) becomes 'Jesus-Mario', as 'pseudomalachi' (9:194) becomes 'false Malachi' and 'Sonmulligan' (9:331) 'Son-Mulligan'. Three entities are reachable in one edition only: BRIAN BORU and LOT'S WIFE in the modern alone, ADAM FINDLATER in the older alone. From episode 8 the modern edition also spells M'Coy as McCOY, which is a third alias on his card.

A SILENT BINDER LIMITATION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY BOOK IN THIS LIBRARY: reviewed_aliases.py guards alias matches with \w, AND AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES \w, so an alias whose occurrence sits inside Gutenberg italics (_like this_) BINDS NOTHING AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. Four cases, all keyed now: '_Los Demiurgos_' 3:1, '_Matcham's Masterstroke_' 4:162, '_That's not Mulcahy_' 6:325, '_Mr MacTrigger_' 8:208 and 8:223. The MacTrigger case was found by the omittedEntities line in the validation report and by nothing else -- read that line on every build. Two of the others were found by the EDITION-ASYMMETRY CENSUS, because the modern edition has no italics; run that census on every episode. Over all 18 episodes the italic check still reports STEPHEN at 15:1133 (a stage direction) and PATRICE at 16:212, which is NOT Patrice Egan but 'the faubourg Saint Patrice'.

A SECOND SILENT FAILURE, FOUND IN EPISODE 8 AND NOW GUARDED: A REPEATED DICT LITERAL IN SPLIT OR PHRASE SHADOWS THE EARLIER ONE AND EVERY KEY IN IT CEASES TO EXIST. A duplicate 'Jack' table had been dropping the episode 7 keys for J. J. O'Molloy, and a duplicate 'Paddy Dignam' table the episode 6 keys, with every test still green. Tables.test_no_split_or_phrase_key_is_declared_twice now parses the source and fails on any repeated key. NEVER RE-DECLARE A TABLE -- MERGE INTO THE EXISTING LITERAL.

DELIBERATELY UNBOUND IN EPISODE 8 AND RECORDED: 'His Majesty the King' 8:0, 'our gracious and popular vicereine' 8:112, 'the old queen in a bathchair' and 'the lord mayor' 8:198, 'the Master of the Rolls' 8:255 -- offices whose holders this episode does not name; 'Albert Edward, Arthur Edmund, Alphonsus Eb Ed El Esquire' 8:144, which is Bloom guessing what A. E. stands for; 'Pen something. Pendennis?' 8:39, which is Bloom failing to recover Penrose's name until 8:355; the Hely's advertising patter 'Hello, Jones... Can't stop, Robinson' 8:35; the voices at 8:172-176; the Burton diners, who are a mass; the racehorses Zinfandel, Sceptre, Saint Amant, Saint Frusquin and John O'Gaunt; and the eponyms 'Pepper's ghost' 8:7 and 'Rontgen rays' 8:322, where the name stands for the thing. Our Saviour carries no card here as everywhere in this package. No edition byte was touched. This lane never sets appStatus.
